conviction_note: abs_move_pct 5.5 is taken from the option-implied move (5.5-5.8% from one aggregator; the baseline sealed empty) and set at that level, above the recent median realised move of about 3.5%, because the release also carries the first guide that includes Crinetics and up to three overdue 2H26 pipeline readouts. p_up is 48: a small revenue lean toward a beat is outweighed by an 11% run-up to an all-time high since 19 October, a whisper above consensus, and a name that paid only +1.7% for a 3.5% revenue beat last quarter. The findings sum to -0.9 and the scaled number is -0.22. Both lean slightly negative and neither is large; the gap between them is simply many small items against one probability tier near 50.
bar: Q3 revenue: $3.40bn (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/408004/vertex-heads-into-q3-with-raised-guidance-as-casgevi-and-gernavix-ramps-face-proof-test), $3.39-3.41bn (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/vrtx/earnings-forecasts) and $3.42bn (247wallst, 2026-10-26, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/the-500-million-non-cf-factor-vertex-investors-cant-ignore-on-nov-2/). These roughly agree, so revenue is the usable bar. Company FY26 guide is $13.1-13.2bn excluding Crinetics, with non-CF revenue of at least $0.5bn (Q2 release, https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). The EPS bar is DISPUTED: $4.92 non-GAAP (Earnings Whispers, whisper $5.10) against -$1.20 (247wallst, range -$29.51 to +$5.06). Some analysts model a Crinetics acquired-IPR&D charge, and Vertex includes AIPR&D in non-GAAP. Every EPS-dependent finding is therefore capped near zero. The FY revenue consensus is also disputed: $13.06bn (EW) against $13.26bn (247wallst).
positioning_check: Short interest 1.56% of float, about 3.9M shares, 3.0 days to cover as of 2026-08-20 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/vrtx/short-interest). The 2026-07-15 settlement was 5.0M shares and 3.1 days (CurvedTrading, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/vrtx/short-interest/). No October settlement was found. This is not a crowded short. Skew: not found; the baseline is empty (bars_failed). Implied move ±5.5% as of 2026-10-29 and ±5.8% as of 2026-11-02 (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move, single source). Price action: close 501.95 on 2026-10-19 and 558.88 on 2026-10-30, a new high above the 555.98 all-time high of 2026-09-02; 548.50 intraday on 2026-11-02 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vrtx/history).

findings.finding: Q3 revenue run-rate inference: Q3 2025 revenue was $3.08bn and Q2 2025 was $2.96bn, so last year's Q2-to-Q3 step was +3.9%. The same step on Q2 2026's $3,333.9M gives about $3.46bn. Separately, CF grew 8% in H1 2026, and 8% on Q3 2025 CF of about $3.04bn plus about $0.16bn of Casgevy, Journavx and one month of Palsonify gives about $3.45bn. Both are about 1-1.5% above the $3.40-3.42bn consensus. Consensus already implies CF growth slowing to about 7%, which management flagged (smaller prior-year US price and FX contribution in H2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $3.33bn against a $3.22bn consensus (+3.5%) with a guide raise; the stock moved +1.7% close-to-close. Q1 2026 was a revenue miss and the stock moved -1.3%. Q3 2025: a small beat with Casgevy short; -1.0%. Sources: https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/the-500-million-non-cf-factor-vertex-investors-cant-ignore-on-nov-2/
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at roughly the H1 growth rate minus the H2 slowdown management signposted, and the whisper ($5.10 against $4.92 EPS) already leans to a beat. If the market fully expected $3.45bn+, the published revenue consensus would have moved off $3.40bn. Earnings Whispers itself frames above $3.45bn as the level that would mean the guide is conservative.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 base and comparison: https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results. This is an inference from the company's own history, not a counterparty number. It shares the Q2 release with the Journavx, FX and guidance findings.

findings.finding: FX swings from a tailwind to a small headwind in Q3. EUR/USD averaged about 1.151 in Q3 2026 (Jul 1.1425, Aug 1.1588, Sep 1.1511) against about 1.169 in Q3 2025 (Jul 1.1680, Aug 1.1640, Sep 1.1735), a weaker euro by about 1.5% YoY. The FY guide assumed about +150bp of FX benefit, earned mostly in H1. Ex-US revenue was $1.28bn of $3.33bn in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No VRTX print traced to FX in the sources found. Management called out FX contributing less in H2 on the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15381606277997568).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management signposted it, and sell-side models hedge FX. What would be different if it were fully priced: consensus would sit near 10% growth rather than about 11%. Hedging (stated in the guide) blunts the effect.
findings.independence: 2025 comparison: https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/EUR-USD-2025. Macro-to-company proxy, not confirmed by the company for Q3.

findings.finding: Journavx Q2 revenue ($49.6M, +71% sequential) was helped by a wholesaler channel build after a Q1 drawdown. Management warned of 'some quarterly volatility in inventory build and drawdown' and pushed gross-to-net normalisation out to H1 2027, with the patient support programme used more than forecast. So Q3 Journavx revenue can lag script growth (Q2 scripts about 535k, +45% sequential) or step down sequentially if the channel unwinds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: Journavx came in just short of expectations ($19.6M) and Casgevy missed ($16.9M against a $35M model); the stock moved -1.0% close-to-close (https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/vertex-confident-journavxs-launch-despite-falling-short-sales, https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews focus on the $500M non-CF target and script momentum (247wallst, Finviz) and do not mention the Q2 channel build. If it were priced, Journavx expectations would be flat sequentially. Net of the rest: Journavx is about 1.5% of revenue, so this matters through the launch narrative, not the total.
findings.independence: Same Q2 call; the Q2 release confirms the revenue and script figures (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). No Q3 IQVIA script data was found.

findings.finding: Casgevy has had three straight quarters of more than 100 patient initiations (through Q2 2026). H1 2026 infusions already exceeded all of 2025, Q2 revenue was $76.4M (+78% sequential), and the CFO said Casgevy is the larger contributor to the 'very confident' $500M+ non-CF target. That needs about $300M in H2 against about $200M in H1. The initiation backlog supports another sequential step in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Casgevy missed in Q3 2025 ($16.9M) and the stock moved -1.0%. Q2 2026's Casgevy acceleration came with a +1.7% move.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the $500M target is the headline every preview carries. What is not in the target is the initiation-to-infusion lag implying Q3 above Q2. Management says timing is variable, so the size is small. Net of the rest: Casgevy is about 2-3% of revenue.
findings.independence: 247wallst repeats the initiation and pediatric-approval figures (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/the-500-million-non-cf-factor-vertex-investors-cant-ignore-on-nov-2/). It shares the call source with the Journavx finding, but they are different products.

findings.finding: The first FY26 guide to include Crinetics (closed 2026-09-01) will add Palsonify revenue (Crinetics Q2 2026 net product revenue $24.0M, Q1 $10.3M, so about $35-40M for Sep-Dec). It will also add Crinetics' cost base (Q2 R&D $99.9M plus SG&A $57.6M, about $157M a quarter, so roughly $200M for Sep-Dec) and interest on the $4.5bn term loan, against the current $5.65-5.75bn non-GAAP opex guide, which Vertex is already tracking at the high end. The headline opex guide will rise, and a revenue raise will be partly inorganic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Vertex print carried an acquisition guide rebase in the sources found. The Alpine deal in 2024 brought a $4.4bn AIPR&D charge (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/vertex-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results references the comparison); its reaction was not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO called the 2026 revenue and opex impact 'relatively modest' and the deal accretive only in 2029, so the direction is signposted. What is not priced is the size: with FY consensus disputed ($13.06bn against $13.26bn), nobody has a clean rebased bar. Financing question answered: the loan buys a marketed product (Palsonify) and a Phase 3 asset; it is not distress.
findings.independence: Deal terms and close: https://pulse2.com/vertex-completes-10-billion-acquisition-of-crinetics-pharmaceuticals/. Deal financing and the 2029 accretion: https://www.webull.com/news/15381606277997568.

findings.finding: The Q3 EPS bar is mechanically broken. Published Q3 consensus reads -$1.20 (range -$29.51 to +$5.06) on 247wallst against $4.92 non-GAAP on Earnings Whispers, because some analysts model a Crinetics acquired-IPR&D charge and Vertex includes AIPR&D in non-GAAP. Whether Crinetics is booked as an asset acquisition (charge) or a business combination (no charge) is not disclosed; Vertex said accounting details come on the Q3 call. The headline beat or miss will be an accounting artefact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not sourced for VRTX. The market has looked through a non-cash AIPR&D charge before (Alpine 2024), but no reaction figure was found.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price: it is a below-operating-income, non-cash item with no path to the guide. It matters only because headline algos and wire copy may print 'beat' or 'miss' against a split consensus in the first minutes, which does not survive to the next close.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers $4.92 / $5.10 whisper: https://finviz.com/news/408004/vertex-heads-into-q3-with-raised-guidance-as-casgevi-and-gernavix-ramps-face-proof-test. Accounting details deferred to the Q3 call: https://www.americanpharmaceuticalreview.com/1315-News/627846-Vertex-Completes-10-Billion-Crinetics-Acquisition-Reshapes-Leadership-Team/

findings.finding: Several 2H26 pipeline readouts promised in the Q2 release have not been reported and may come with the Q3 release or call: VX-828 next-generation CF proof of concept (Phase 1 NCT06154447 primary completion 2026-07-10), VX-670 DM1 GALILEO results ('complete dosing and share results in 2H26'), and updated zimislecel / VX-017 type 1 diabetes timelines ('later this year'). The sign is unknown; this widens the distribution.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 4 2025: a pipeline disappointment (pain) alongside the print gave -20.6% close-to-close against a 6.6% implied move (https://earnings-watcher.com/wiki/vrtx-implied-move). Pipeline news on print day has been the tail driver for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Unknown outcome. Options price ±5.5-5.8%, which is above the recent median realised move and probably carries some of this. There is no sign to price.
findings.independence: VX-670 timing confirmed by partner Entrada's Q2 2026 report (https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/entrada-therapeutics-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results). Milestone list from Vertex's Q2 release.

findings.finding: Run-up and informal bar: VRTX rose from 501.95 (2026-10-19 close) to 558.88 (2026-10-30 close, +11.3%), above its 2026-09-02 all-time high of 555.98, helped by RAINIER Phase 3 povetacicept data in NEJM and at ASN on 2026-10-24 (PDUFA 2026-11-30). The whisper EPS of $5.10 sits above the $4.92 consensus. The stock goes into the print with a raised informal bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: up about 11% into the print window per Earnings Whispers, then +1.7% on a beat and raise. Beats have been bought modestly, not strongly.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the market pricing good news; the point is that it raises the bar the print must clear. If the market expected a plain in-line quarter, the stock would not sit at an all-time high with a whisper above consensus. Short interest of 1.56% of float means no squeeze cushion.

findings.finding: The FY revenue consensus may already sit above the guide top. 247wallst carries FY26 consensus at $13.26bn against the $13.1-13.2bn guide (EW carries $13.06bn). Q4 2025 implied about $3.19bn (FY25 $12.00bn less H1 $5.735bn less Q3 $3.08bn), +3.4% on Q3 2025. The same seasonality on a $3.42bn Q3 gives about $13.28bn. An organic guide raise is likely, but if the $13.26bn figure is right it is already in the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raises: Q2 2026 raise +1.7%; Feb 2026 print +5.7%. No miss-on-guide print found in the sources.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is disputed between two sources, so the market's real expectation for the guide is unclear. Capped small under the bar rule.
findings.independence: EW's lower FY figure (https://finviz.com/news/408004/vertex-heads-into-q3-with-raised-guidance-as-casgevi-and-gernavix-ramps-face-proof-test) cuts the other way. This shares the Q3-2025 arithmetic with the revenue finding but answers a different question (the guide, not the quarter).

findings.finding: BofA forecasts Q3 Trikafta at $2.42bn, 5% below consensus. Trikafta fell about 2% YoY in Q2 ($2,497.2M) as patients switched to Alyftrek ($573.6M, +35% sequential), so a Trikafta shortfall is largely offset inside total CF.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not sourced at the product line level.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side view already published. Net of the rest: the Alyftrek switch takes up the Trikafta shortfall, so the total-CF effect is near zero.

baseline_tension: There is no sealed skew or history. The evidence is a slight revenue beat lean against an 11% run-up to an all-time high and a whisper above consensus. These roughly cancel, and the run-up argues the good news is largely in the price.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction; Q2's 3.5% beat bought +1.7%): revenue inference cut from +0.6 to +0.4; print_vs_bar cut from +0.6 to +0.5
Lesson 9 (size a segment net of the rest): Journavx -0.4 to -0.3, Casgevy +0.3 to +0.2, Trikafta -0.1 to 0.0 (Alyftrek switch offsets it)
Lesson 6 (disputed bar): FY consensus finding capped -0.3 to -0.2; EPS-bar finding kept at 0
Lesson 4 (financing is a question) and the 'inside what was guided' rule: the Crinetics guide/opex item is signposted as 'relatively modest' by the CFO, so -0.3 to -0.2
Lesson 7: short interest checked (1.56% float, 3 days), not crowded, so negatives not shrunk for a squeeze; no skew available
